reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that coherent γ/γ′ interfaces in HESAs block dislocations and improve creep resistance, and that moderate misfit enhances coherency. However, it does not provide any data on FCC/BCC interfaces, nor does it address whether controlled cooling can enhance coherency in such systems. The key premise that these mechanisms transfer to FCC/BCC HEA coatings is therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Coherent and strongly bonded FCC/BCC interfaces act as effective barriers to dislocation motion and atomic diffusion
Enhanced interface coherency reduces steady-state creep rate and extends time to failure
The relationship between interface misfit/coherency and creep resistance is transferable from γ/γ′ systems to FCC/BCC HEA coatings
Processing via controlled cooling rates can systematically enhance FCC/BCC interface coherency and bonding strength
